label: Make a mark
heading: Now make it
intro: In the Pain, Felt and Drawn workshop, people were asked to imagine a day at the beach: picking up a shell, the sharp edge that cuts a finger, the pain, and the healing. This is that exercise, online. Every word from [Take part](#takepart) is a brush here. Choose a word and your hand makes it.
disclaimer: Nothing you make here is stored or sent anywhere. Save it if you want to keep it.
guide_source: The prompts are from the Pain, Felt and Drawn workshop at the Archives at NCBS. Follow them or ignore them: the words and colours are yours.

steps.title: The touch
steps.prompt: You are walking along a beach, collecting shells. Feel one in your hand, and the sand and water under your foot. What does that sensation look like?

steps.title: The cut
steps.prompt: The sharp edge of a shell cuts your finger. How would that sensation look?

steps.title: The pain, and the healing
steps.prompt: The pain stays for a while, and then there is healing. What softens, and what stays? You can blend what you made, or leave it as a scar.

tools_label: Or work on what is there
modulate_hint: Modulate — blends and softens what you have already made. It is the word neuroscience uses for turning pain down, and the word painters use for smoothing a hard edge.
lift_hint: Lift — takes the colour back off, down to the paper.

reflections.title: What your hand did

feels.text: Most of what you made is about **how it feels on the body**: pressure, heat, cold, the skin's own reading of the world. That is the territory of the somatosensory system, which responds to the most diverse set of stimuli in the body: mechanical, thermal and chemical.

moves.text: Most of what you made is about **how it moves**: whether it pulses, creeps or comes and goes. How a sensation changes over time is one of the things body mapping exists to capture, and a number from one to ten cannot.

does.text: Most of what you made is about **what it does to you**, not only how it feels. The exhibition note calls this the emotional burden of pain: substantial, and the part most treatments are not designed to address.

mixed.text: Your marks cover how it feels, how it moves and what it does to you. That is the whole of it, and exactly what a number from one to ten leaves out.

modulated.text: You also softened what you made. *Modulating* is the word neuroscience textbooks use for turning pain down. In painting, it means blending a rough edge into its surroundings.
